segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and kept back for himself some of the proceeds, with his wife also aware of it; and he brought a part of it and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back for yourself some of the proceeds of the land?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: While it remained unsold, did it not remain yours? And once it was sold, was it not under your own authority? How is it that you conceived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to human beings but to God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all who heard of it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The younger men got up, wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After an interval of about three hours his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said to her,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Tell me, did you two sell the land for this much?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Yes, for this much.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Peter said to her,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How is it that you two agreed to put the Spirit of the Lord to the test? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And great fear came upon the whole assembly and upon all who heard of these things.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Many signs and wonders were being done among the people through the hands of the apostles. And they were all together, of one mind, in Solomon’s Colonnade.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: None of the rest dared to join them, but the people held them in high esteem,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and more than ever believers in the Lord were added, crowds of both men and women,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, in order that when Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A crowd also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the high priest rose up, along with all who were with him—that is, the party of the Sadducees—and they were filled with jealousy

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and seized the apostles and put them in public custody.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, led them out, and said,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Go, stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this, they went into the temple at daybreak and began teaching. Meanwhile the high priest and those with him arrived, called together the council and the whole body of elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the jail to have them brought.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the officers arrived, they did not find them in the prison. They returned and reported,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We found the jail locked up quite securely and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them we found no one inside.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were completely at a loss about them, wondering what this might come to.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then someone arrived and reported to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look! The men you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the captain went off with the officers and brought them, but not by force, for they were afraid of being stoned by the people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had brought them, they stood them before the council. The high priest questioned them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name, and look—you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to bring this man’s blood upon us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter and the apostles answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We must obey God rather than human beings.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you put to death by hanging him on a tree.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: God exalted this man to his right hand as Leader and Savior, to grant Israel turning back and forgiveness of sins.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this, they were enraged and wanted to kill them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the Law honored by all the people, stood up in the council and ordered the men to be put outside for a little while.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Men of Israel, take care what you are about to do with these men.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men rallied to him. He was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew people away after him. He too perished, and all who followed him were scattered.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So in the present case I tell you: stay away from these men and leave them alone. For if this plan or this undertaking is of human origin, it will be overthrown;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them. Otherwise you may even be found fighting against God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were persuaded by him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and after calling in the apostles and having them flogged, they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus and released them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they went out from the presence of the council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to be dishonored for the sake of the name.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and announcing the good news that the Messiah is Jesus.

notes.note: The Greek verb means to misappropriate or skim off for oneself. It is the verb the Greek Old Testament uses of Achan, who secretly took devoted plunder at Jericho (Joshua 7:1), and many scholars think the echo is intended. As verse 4 makes clear, the offense was not keeping some of the money, which was his to keep, but pretending to hand over all of it.

notes.phrase: put the Spirit of the Lord to the test
notes.traditional: tempt the Spirit of the Lord
notes.note: The verb means to put to the test, and in the Greek Old Testament it is the regular word for Israel testing God in the wilderness. Older English versions have “tempt,” which now suggests enticing someone to sin; most modern translations use “test” here.

This is the first use of the word in Acts in the earliest manuscripts. A first-century reader knew it as the term for a civic gathering and as the Greek Old Testament’s word for Israel assembled before God. “Church” is the near-universal rendering and readers know what it refers to, but it now suggests a building or an institution, so “assembly” is used throughout this translation.

notes.traditional: of the rest durst no man join himself to them
notes.note: The Greek does not say who “the rest” are. They may be outsiders who admired the believers but kept a wary distance after the deaths of Ananias and Sapphira, or other believers who did not presume to attach themselves to the apostles. The first reading sits in some tension with verse 14, and interpreters remain divided.

notes.phrase: believers in the Lord were added
notes.traditional: believers were the more added to the Lord
notes.note: The words “the Lord” can go with either verb: “those believing in the Lord were added” or “believers were added to the Lord.” Both are grammatical, and translations are split between them.

The Greek word covers both envy and zeal. Most translations take it as jealousy of the apostles’ popularity. It could also be religious zeal, the indignation of men who believed they were defending God’s honor.

notes.phrase: the council and the whole body of elders of the sons of Israel
notes.traditional: the council and all the senate of the children of Israel
notes.note: The council is the Sanhedrin, the supreme Jewish court in Jerusalem, presided over by the high priest. The “and” may be explanatory (“the council, that is, the whole body of elders”), since no second governing body is known. The solemn phrasing echoes Old Testament language for Israel’s elders.

The Greek word means wood or anything made of it, and here refers to the cross. The phrase echoes Deuteronomy 21:22–23, where a man hanged on a tree is under God’s curse. The apostles’ wording therefore sharpens the charge: the council treated as accursed the one whom God then exalted.

The traditional rendering is “repentance,” which most translations keep as an established term. In modern English that word centers on feeling sorry, whereas the Greek carries the prophets’ call for Israel to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct. “Turning back” is used for this word group throughout this translation.

The Jewish historian Josephus describes a Theudas whose movement was crushed under the governor Fadus, around AD 44–46. That is some years after this scene and decades after Judas the Galilean, whose revolt at the census of AD 6 Gamaliel places later. Either the chronology here differs from that of Josephus, or an otherwise unknown earlier Theudas is meant; scholars are divided.

notes.phrase: the good news that the Messiah is Jesus
notes.note: The Greek has the article with “Christ,” which marks it here as a title rather than part of a name, so “Messiah” is used. The phrase can be read “that the Messiah is Jesus” or “Jesus as the Messiah”; older versions have simply “Jesus Christ.” The verb, traditionally “preach” or “preach the gospel,” is the ordinary word for announcing good news.

candidates.reason: Translations vary between “council” and the loanword “Sanhedrin” across the Gospels and Acts, and readers should see one term for the one body.
Rendered variously as “Prince,” “Author,” “Leader,” “pioneer” or “founder” in Acts 3:15, 5:31 and Hebrews 2:10, 12:2; one decision is needed for a Christological title.
The singular/plural split between “high priest” and “chief priests” hides that it is one Greek word and should be fixed uniformly across the Gospels, Acts and Hebrews.
Used of Sadducees, Pharisees and the Jesus movement in Acts and of factions in the letters; “sect,” “party,” “faction” and “heresy” carry very different connotations.
Recurs across the Gospels, Acts and the letters as “forgiveness,” “remission” or “release,” and the Jubilee “release” sense in Luke 4:18 makes a consistent policy desirable.
